abstract: This review of empirical evidence examines AI's impact on labor markets, finding that AI-exposed occupations have experienced no measurable change in job openings or aggregate employment. Rather than broad workforce displacement, the evidence suggests labor market adjustment is occurring through task reallocation within existing positions, indicating a more nuanced relationship between AI adoption and employment outcomes than simple job elimination models predict.
keyFindings: No measurable change in job openings in AI-exposed occupations
No measurable change in aggregate employment in AI-exposed occupations
Labor market adjustment is happening through task reallocation rather than broad displacement
